propositions: The parent-first cascade walk logic is implemented twice (in claim.py and transition.py) with byte-identical ghost/init preconditions, creating maintenance and bug-reintroduction risk.

The claim implementation hardcodes only the open→in_progress edge while transition supports three edges (open→in_progress, closed→open, closed→in_progress) via a decision table, leading to incomplete cascade coverage.

A shared cascade_parent_first function must extract the ancestor recursion, cycle guard, benign-race TOCTOU check, and ConcurrencyMismatch error rewrap without moving the _CASCADING_EDGES decision table, which inbound writers already single-source.
The three cascading edges must all remain working after extraction, and the cascade=False replay suppression must be preserved at the seam.
The reopen transition already cascades via the (closed→open) table row and must keep working after consolidation.
